_comment: COUPLING tier-2, FSI with the structure in 4C. The second cross-code FSI pair, and the one that establishes the capability against an established code: FEniCSx ALE Navier-Stokes under the conda fenics interpreter against a 4C plane-strain WALL QUAD4 plate driven by a plain-Python wrapper that writes an inline-mesh 4C deck, runs the binary, and reads the VTU back. Measured 2026-08-07 through the public `couple` tool, 160x16 4C plate against a 48x10 fluid (161 structure interface points against 49 fluid ones, non-matching): converged in 20 iterations to a residual of 3.69e-10, validation EMPTY, interface equilibrium 3.698e-05 (x) / 6.424e-05 (y) componentwise, kinematic continuity 2.408e-14 / 2.753e-13 componentwise, and 4.817e-10 relative L2 against the Newton-Krylov re-solve of the same coupled interface equation. Interface sensitivities S = 0.375 (fluid) and 0.999 (4C), both far above the response floor, so both directions are live. max|dy| = 1.055710358e-02 against the scikit-fem structure's 1.059485302e-02 under the same fluid, a difference of 0.356%; a FEniCSx structure gives 1.059505430e-02. Three structure discretisations in three codes sharing no library, all within 0.36% of each other. The residual 0.36% is 4C's WALL QUAD4 shear locking, measured independently against a converged scikit-fem plate under the SAME analytic load at -7.6% (48x4), -2.1% (96x8) and -0.38% (160x16). One bug was found here and only here: the 4C participant reported its applied traction by re-evaluating the expression TEXT it emitted into the deck, and on iteration 1 that expression is a CONSTANT, so eval returned a scalar and normal_fluxes came out as ONE point against 41 displacements. The driver refused at iteration 2 with 'participant solid changed its export length from 84 to 164'. A standalone run of the participant cannot see it, and the participant's own standalone verification passed.

_mutation.note: Coarsen the 4C plate to 40x4, the mesh at which its bilinear QUAD4 shear-locks hardest. The coupling still converges, still balances, still satisfies kinematic continuity, and the Newton-Krylov reference still finds the root — the run is internally impeccable and 4C is simply solving a stiffer plate than the one asked for. fourc_agrees_with_skfem is what sees it: the cross-code comparison is the only check in this fixture that can, which is the point of having a third code at all. The size of the gap on the mutant is not stated here because it was not measured — what was measured is that the fixture went red and that this is the only assertion that could have taken it there. VERIFIED 2026-08-07: killed. Base run the same day: failures_count=0, fourc_vs_skfem_rel=0.003563.
